title: The Radio Never Goes Quiet
tagline: A ten-hour patrol, a call that could be nothing or everything, and a radio that never really lets you relax.

wake_up.text: Roll call is at 6:30. Your vest still smells like yesterday's coffee, and today's briefing mentions a rash of car break-ins on your beat.

choices.text: Do a full check of your gear before roll call
Quick check — you know it's fine

roll_call.text: Sergeant runs through the overnight incident log and today's watch priorities. Your partner is already waiting by the cruiser.

choices.text: Head out on patrol

random_moment.text: The first hour of a shift always settles into its own rhythm — quiet streets, a little different every day.

choices.text: A shop owner you know waves you down just to say hello
Dispatch radio cuts to static for an uneasy minute
You catch the diner on your route at exactly the right moment for coffee

traffic_stop.text: A routine traffic stop for a broken taillight. The driver is fidgety, avoiding eye contact — could be nothing, could be something.

choices.text: Take the extra time to do it by the book, fully
Give a quick warning and move on

morning_patrol.text: Back on patrol. The break-ins from this morning's briefing are still bothering you — something about the pattern doesn't add up yet.

choices.text: Keep patrolling

domestic_call.text: Dispatch: a domestic disturbance call, neighbors reporting shouting. You arrive to raised voices behind the door and no way to know what's actually happening inside until you're through it.

choices.text: Knock and enter immediately to assess the situation
Wait outside the door and listen before entering
Call for backup before doing anything else
Announce yourself calmly and try to talk them down through the door first

domestic_outcome_immediate.text: You're through the door fast. It turns out to be a heated argument, nothing physical — your quick presence is what actually ends it, before it could become something worse.

choices.text: De-escalate and file the report

domestic_outcome_wait.text: The extra thirty seconds tells you exactly what you're walking into before you have to. You go in prepared, and it makes all the difference in how calmly it resolves.

choices.text: De-escalate and file the report

domestic_outcome_backup.text: Backup arrives in six minutes. By the time you go in together, the shouting has already stopped on its own — six minutes that, this time, you didn't actually need.

choices.text: Check on the household

domestic_outcome_talk.text: Your voice through the door, calm and steady, does more than a fast entry would have. By the time the door opens, most of the tension already has.

choices.text: De-escalate and file the report

lunch_break.text: A short window for lunch, if the radio stays quiet long enough to actually eat it.

choices.text: Actually sit down and eat
Eat in the cruiser, staying available

afternoon_patrol.text: A store owner flags you down: security footage shows the same car from three of this week's break-ins, parked outside right now.

choices.text: Approach the vehicle immediately
Observe from a distance and call in the plate first

school_zone.text: School lets out. Traffic control duty at the crosswalk, a hundred kids at once, and a driver clearly not paying attention approaching the intersection.

choices.text: Step in firmly to stop traffic before it's a problem
Signal normally and trust drivers to stop

evening_report.text: Paperwork for the day's calls, the part of the job that never quite gets easier no matter how many years in.

choices.text: Write thorough, detailed reports on everything
Keep the reports brief and get to end of shift

end_shift.text: Shift change. The next watch takes the radio, and whatever the night brings isn't yours to answer anymore.

choices.text: Clock out

triumphant.title: Textbook Watch
triumphant.blurb: Every call today was handled exactly right, including the one that could have gone very differently. This is the shift the department talks about.

steady_hand.title: Solid Shift
steady_hand.blurb: No headlines, no incidents that needed explaining. Just careful, competent police work, call after call.

ordinary_day.title: Routine Patrol
ordinary_day.blurb: A normal ten hours on the beat. Tomorrow's watch looks about the same.

burned_out.title: Running on Empty
burned_out.blurb: You made it to end of shift, but you're not sure how. Call after call, this pace has a real cost.

written_up.title: Under Review
written_up.blurb: A few of today's calls are heading into a formal review. Nobody was hurt. The department still wants answers.
